children: TOKYO--Japan's consumer inflation remained near the central bank's 2% target, while the Bank of Japan is widely expected to raise interest rates later in the day to curb persistent price pressures.
Consumer prices, excluding fresh food, climbed 1.7% in August from a year earlier, slightly slower than July's 1.8% increase but holding close to the BOJ's target, government data showed Friday.
The results came just hours before the BOJ concludes its closely watched policy-setting meeting, where decision makers are expected to raise the benchmark rate by 25 basis points, to 1.25%.

With markets almost fully pricing in a September increase, focus has already shifted to how quickly the BOJ will act next. BOJ policymakers have cited the effects of the Middle East conflict, yen fluctuations, and demand related to artificial intelligence as potential factors pushing up inflation.
In a sign of solid underlying inflation, the measure that strips out both fresh food and energy prices rose 1.9% on the year in August, matching the pace recorded in July, Friday's data showed.
The overnight index swaps market is pricing in roughly a 65% chance of an additional interest-rate increase by the end of the year.
